name: @projexlight/sdk-identity-resolver
summary: Identity-resolution layer for ProjexCloud: given a partial signal (email, phone, anonymous device cookie, IP block, Salesforce contact id), return the canonical persona + the resolution explanation (what fields matched, what confidence, which version of the matching rules). Foundation for any 'who is this' workflow — anonymous-visitor-to-known-contact, multi-channel attribution, de-duplication.

endpoints.description: Resolve a signal bundle to the most-likely persona; returns persona_id + confidence + matched fields.
Explain a past resolution — which rules fired, which fields matched.

events.name: identity-resolver.resolution.v1
events.description: Per-resolution row: input signals, resolved persona, matched_rules_json, confidence.

events.name: identity-resolver.merge.suggested.v1
events.description: Two distinct personas look like they should merge (high cross-match confidence). Suggested, not applied — operator confirms.

hooks.name: resolve
hooks.description: Resolve a signal bundle to a persona; returns persona_id + confidence + matched fields.

hooks.name: explain
hooks.description: Explain a past resolution: which rules fired, which fields matched, which confidence threshold applied.

scenarios.title: Anonymous web visitor converts → resolve to existing contact
scenarios.when_to_use: Visitor filled a form with their email; resolver matches the email + the device cookie to an existing contact, attributing past sessions retroactively.
scenarios.expected_outcome: Returns existing persona + confidence + matched fields. Past anonymous sessions retroactively attributed.

scenarios.title: Inbound call → resolve from phone number
scenarios.when_to_use: Inbound voice call; we have only the phone number — resolver matches against contact + lead phone fields.
scenarios.expected_outcome: Best-match persona returned. Below RESOLVER_CONFIDENCE_AUTO_THRESHOLD the caller decides whether to act.

scenarios.title: Customer-success rep asks: why did we attribute this session to Alice?
scenarios.when_to_use: Reviewer wants the trail for any past resolution — explain returns the rules that fired + which fields matched + the rule-set version at the time.
scenarios.expected_outcome: Full reproducible trace. Sufficient for GDPR Art-22 + EU AI Act explainability.

scenarios.title: Two contacts look like the same person → merge suggested
scenarios.when_to_use: Same email-pattern + similar names + overlapping company; resolver flags as merge candidate (not auto-applied — operator confirms).
scenarios.expected_outcome: Operator reviews + accepts/rejects. Accepted merges flow through sdk-crm's merge path.

scenarios.title: Resolve a Salesforce contact ID → ProjexCloud persona
scenarios.when_to_use: Inbound from connector-salesforce — we receive an SF Contact ID and need the matching ProjexCloud persona to attach activity.
scenarios.expected_outcome: Direct match via the external_id mapping; high confidence. Caller attaches activity to the resolved persona.

compliance_posture.notes: Every resolution pinned to the rule-set version + the matched fields, so a regulator can replay how an identity was inferred. Merge suggestions never auto-apply for high-stakes verticals (healthcare / finserv) — operator confirmation required.
